acceptable_changes: Cut the Marlborough House alternative (para 4) and most of the London-delights catalogue (para 5). Both were marked optional.
Added a brief source-backed gloss identifying the Gold Conspiracy as the Gould/Fisk/Erie gold-scandal essay meant for Reeve and the Edinburgh Review, because Chapter 020 is omitted.
Added a gloss for the Session article as a review of the 1869-70 session of Congress.
Reduced the Louis XIV/Napoleon war-as-art lineage to one sentence.
Folded the press verdict (para 23) into a single sentence and cut the Pendleton/Sherman qualifiers and the hypothetical careers list.
Cut paragraph 25's argument down to its closing rhetorical questions, which keep the Washington-loved/Cambridge-shunned contrast.
Compressed the railway-station vignette but kept the Fisk/Gould contrast and the cards/whiskey ending.
review_focus: Gold Conspiracy gloss wording against the omitted chapter's evidence.
Pairing of Adams's 'I know nothing about Mediaeval History' with Eliot's reply, each in its own paragraph.
The transition from the Hewitt surveys remark to the Harvard-versus-Washington questions.
risks: Length is estimated, not measured, and may deviate somewhat from 2700.
The bridge 'Among the men at Washington' compresses Adams's claim to know all prominent men there.
The gloss on the Session article ('review of the session of Congress of 1869-70') is supplied from the plan, not from this chapter.
summary: Abridgment of CHAOS (1870) that keeps the six-section arc. It runs from the London return and the rococo mood, through the Gold Conspiracy refusals, the sister's death and the vision of Nature, Ouchy, the Paris war and Wenlock, to the begonia, the family pressure, the Eliot exchange, and the closing verdict on Washington and the American character. All eight verbatim excerpts are kept.
